summary: Iter78 InvoiceCreate customer picker (AsyncSearchableSelect) tested end-to-end on desktop (1920x1080) and mobile (390x844). The frontend replacement of the native <select> works correctly: picker opens a debounced search box, typing 'MEGHA' returns the single real customer MEGHA ENGINEERING, typing 'C-9' returns C-945254; selecting an option sets customer_id, triggers /api/trips?customer_id=..., and the picker button shows the customer's name (not raw id). Clear button resets both the picker and the trips list. Voice button flow was code-reviewed (setCustomerId(p.customer_id) is called; combined with the ids-lookup useQuery the picker will refresh to the name). ONE bug found on the backend fixture filter: the iter70 FIXTURE_NAME_REGEX does not catch names starting with 'CUST_IT<digits>_' (e.g. CUST_IT56_*, CUST_IT59_*). With an empty query, ~40% of the first 50 paginated customers were CUST_IT* fixture pollution. Text-search paths (name/phone/GSTIN) are clean because they usually match zero fixtures; the leak is only visible when the user opens the picker without typing.

minor.issue: Iter70 fixture filter regex ^(IT\d+|TEST[_-]|IsoCoB|Iso_|BULK_|Bulk_|Cust_[a-f0-9]{6}) does NOT match names like 'CUST_IT56_df71f5' or 'CUST_IT59_42964a' which are clearly pytest fixture customers. Result: 20/50 (~40%) of first-page browse results are fixture pollution when picker is opened with no search term. Fix: extend FIXTURE_NAME_REGEX to also match ^CUST_IT\d+_ (and consider case-insensitive Cust_/CUST_ hex variant). File: /app/backend/routers/customers.py line 36.

action_items: Extend backend FIXTURE_NAME_REGEX in /app/backend/routers/customers.py to also hide 'CUST_IT\d+_' fixture customers (add alternation, e.g. |CUST_IT\d+_). Also consider making the Cust_[a-f0-9]{6} variant case-insensitive so 'CUST_' uppercase hex fixtures are covered.
critical_code_review_comments: InvoiceCreate.jsx still calls the legacy `useQuery(['customers'])` fetching ALL customers just so `selectedCustomer` can fall back to that array. Now that the ids-lookup useQuery handles selected-customer resolution, the full list fetch can be removed to save one large payload per page load.

Iter70 fixture regex is anchored at start-of-name and misses the widely-used 'CUST_IT<n>_<hex>' fixture pattern generated by newer iteration tests (IT56, IT59). This regex will drift; consider tagging fixture customers with an explicit boolean field (e.g. is_fixture: true) instead of relying on name pattern matching.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter78 frontend change (AsyncSearchableSelect in InvoiceCreate) is fully working. Only remaining item is to extend the backend fixture-name regex to hide CUST_IT* names in paginated browse. After that, re-open the picker with no search term and confirm the first page contains only real customer names.
